# Churn Is Dead: full issue corpus

> 46 published Customer Success issues by Kuber Sethi, grouped by the operating problem each addresses. Each entry is a stable canonical URL suitable for citation. Generated from the live catalog.

Attribution: cite as Kuber Sethi, Churn Is Dead (churnisdead.com). The newsletter's position is evidence-led: it distinguishes what CS controls from what it does not, and prefers one defensible argument over broad advice.

## Renewal economics: what CS controls versus pricing and contract mechanics
- [The Renewal Is Not Yours to Own. The Change Order Is.](https://churnisdead.com/newsletter/renewal-not-yours-change-order-is): CS imported professional services' 'do whatever it takes' ethos and left behind the one discipline that made it survivable: the change order.
- [You Don't Own NRR. You Rent It From Pricing.](https://churnisdead.com/newsletter/you-dont-own-nrr-you-rent-it-from-pricing): Most of your NRR is inherited from the pricing model, not earned by your team. Here's how to prove it, and how to earn a seat in the room that actually moves the number.
- [The Renewal Clause Your Lawyers Wrote and Your CS Team Forgot](https://churnisdead.com/newsletter/renewal-clause-lawyers-wrote-cs-forgot): The fastest NRR in your portfolio this year isn't in your expansion pipeline. It's in your filing cabinet, in the escalator clause nobody enforced.

## Measurement that changes a decision, not decorative dashboards
- [The Renewal Cliff Nobody Charted: Why CS Doesn't Own Half the Churn It's Blamed For](https://churnisdead.com/newsletter/renewal-cliff-data-intelligence-blind-spot): Your churn model isn't getting smarter. It's getting more confident about the half of the problem it can see, and staying blind to the half that kills renewals.
- [The 30-Minute Monthly Business Review](https://churnisdead.com/newsletter/fire-your-qbr-heres-what-to-do-instead): QBRs waste executive time by reporting on history instead of driving decisions. Here's the Monthly Business Review that actually moves the needle.
- [Your CS Metrics Are Performance Theater](https://churnisdead.com/newsletter/cs-metrics-performance-theater): Most CS metrics measure motion, not progress. Here's how to spot the difference and build measurements that actually drive retention.

## Redesigning CS work around defensible judgment in the age of AI
- [The CSM Title Is Now a Liability. The Rebrand Everyone's Reaching For Won't Fix It.](https://churnisdead.com/newsletter/csm-title-liability-rebrand-wont-fix-it): Renaming your CSMs to Forward Deployed Engineers fixes your recruiting funnel and moves your credibility gap to the exact place the customer finds it later: the renewal.
- [Your AI Customer Success Strategy Is Actually Firing People](https://churnisdead.com/newsletter/ai-customer-success-firing-people): CS leaders are using AI transformation as cover for headcount reduction while selling it as productivity enhancement.
- [AI Won't Save Customer Success. It'll Finish It Off.](https://churnisdead.com/newsletter/ai-wont-save-customer-success): AI isn't elevating the CSM role. It's exposing how hollow most of it was. Here's the AI Exposure Framework — 4 questions that determine whether your role survives automation.

You're documenting a decision made three quarters ago, during the one phase you actually contr
- [The Two-Vendor Trick: How CS Platforms Quietly Became Org Charts You Can't Edit](https://churnisdead.com/newsletter/cs-platform-org-chart-you-cant-edit): You bought a CS platform to operationalize your strategy. Instead it operationalized the vendor's. Here's how to find out which decisions you never actually made.
- [Stop Scheduling Success: The Continuous CS Operating Model](https://churnisdead.com/newsletter/fire-your-qbr-what-to-do-instead): QBRs are elaborate customer success theater. The highest-retention SaaS companies deliver success through continuous, in-product experiences instead.

## Alternatives to blended customer health scores
- [The Case Against Customer Health Scores](https://churnisdead.com/newsletter/case-against-customer-health-scores): Health scores are the astrology of customer success—providing false confidence while real churn drivers remain invisible.
- [Health Scores Are Astrology for CS Teams](https://churnisdead.com/newsletter/health-scores-are-astrology): Your greenest account just decided to leave and your dashboard has no idea. Here's the 7-lens framework that replaces health scores with actual predictability.
- [Usage Is Not Success](https://churnisdead.com/newsletter/usage-is-not-success): High usage doesn’t guarantee renewal. In this issue, we break down why usage ≠ success and how to connect activity to outcomes that actually drive retention. Includes a 1-slide QBR
